citation: A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885), pp. 69-70 ('Water Works') and p. 742 (the fire at the works).
author: A. T. Andreas
locator: Vol. 2, pp. 69-70: the engine house 142 by 60 feet and 36 feet in the clear, castellated Gothic in rock-faced ashlar with cut-stone trimmings, the slate roof on massive timbers, the two-storey centre of the main front round the main entrance, the boiler rooms nineteen feet apart in the rear and the 130-foot smoke-stack between them; the tower about one hundred feet west of the main building, its octagonal shaft to a battlemented cornice at 154 feet, the iron cupola, the forty-foot base and the 36-inch stand-pipe 138 feet high. P. 742: the works' roof caught at about 3:20 a.m. on 9 October and fell; the tower was only slightly damaged.
rights_note: Published 1885 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-20 (T-3689) from the Internet Archive's OCR text and page images of pp. 69-70 and 742.
note: Written fourteen years after the fire from the city's records; the dimensions agree with HABS's survey of the tower.
what_it_supplies: the works' plan dimensions, style, material and roof
the tower's heights and its distance from the works
when the works' roof burned and that the tower survived
what_it_does_not_supply: the works' orientation on its lot (read from the stereographs)
